decisions.rationale: The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 500-623 exactly state that the album begins with "Dark Fantasy" opened by Nicki Minaj narrating a rework of Roald Dahl's 1982 poem Cinderella.
The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 1173-1219 exactly describe "Gorgeous" as an uplifting blues-styled track.
The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 1513-1625 exactly state that "Power" has dark production relying on a King Crimson "21st Century Schizoid Man" sample.

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 500-639 exactly state that the song is often played with "All of the Lights (Interlude)", which precedes it on the album tracklist.

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 2169-2308 exactly state that West enlisted 11 guest vocalists including the named artists and that Rihanna sings the hook.
The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 2608-2633 exactly describe "Monster" as a posse cut.
The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 2953-3022 exactly describe "So Appalled" as a fellow posse cut built around piano and strings.

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 3811-3911 exactly state that "Devil in a New Dress" is built on a sample of Smokey Robinson's "Will You Love Me Tomorrow" (1960).

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 4287-4395 exactly state that "Runaway" contains a piano-based motif made of uninterrupted descending half and whole notes.

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 5031-5157 exactly state that "Hell of a Life" was inspired by West's two-year relationship with Amber Rose and samples the Mojo Men's "She's My Baby" (1966).

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 5548-5670 exactly state that "Blame Game" is a low-key track built around a sample of Richard D. James's "Avril 14th" (2001).

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 5904-6019 exactly state that "Lost in the World" features tribal drums and prominent samples from Bon Iver's "Woods" (2009).

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 6536-6629 state that the track serves as the album's coda and samples Gil Scott-Heron's "Comment No. 1" (1970); the immediately preceding retainedText identifies the track as "Who Will Survive in America".

The artifact exists, its canonical URL matches the sourceRef URL, and offsets 500-664 exactly state that the album version includes a Big Sean verse and appears on My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy (2010) as an iTunes Store bonus track.
